text:
incident-bot: URGENT: Observability ingestion delay detected (Datadog) in us-east-1. Metric/log/tracing ingestion latency > 4m for 12m. Potential monitoring blindspot. Paging @oncall-sre. :rotating_light:

alex: got it, joining. Noticed missing spans and a handful of alerts that didn't enrich with host tags. Which pipelines are affected?

rina: log pipeline A + trace pipeline B showing backpressure. Our forwarder (logship-1) queue at ~120k events. infra_bot shows increased 502s from datadog-ingest.us-east-1.datadog.net.

alex: running quick checks:
```
# forwarder queue
curl -s http://logship-1.internal:8080/queue | jq '.size, .backpressure'
# pod status
kubectl -n observability get pods -l app=logship -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.containerStatuses[*].restartCount}'
```

alex: restarts=0, queue size 123456, backpressure=true. Not restarting pods because we don't want to lose the buffer.

tom: datadog-support-bot posted an update: "Investigating increased tail latency in ingestion cluster us-east-1 due to partial worker outage." ETA 35-70m.

cs_manager: alerting CS: we'll notify customers who have active tickets. @rina please compile list.

rina: list: beta-hospitality (active incident), neoanalytics (support-inquiry), corefin (no active tickets). beta-hospitality uses real-time traces for payment flows. High risk.

alex: mitigation options:
- retain buffer & apply sampling/filtering to reduce queue pressure
- drop non-essential debug logs at source
- temporarily route logs to S3 (archive) for replay once Datadog catches up
- flip critical alerts to our internal prometheus endpoints for redundancy


tom: I'm in favor of S3 sink + sampling. If we keep buffer too long we risk OOM. Do we have playbook for on-the-fly S3 route?

alex: we have a script but not in runbook. Quick command to enable streaming:
```
kubectl -n observability exec deploy/logship -- /bin/sh -c "enable-s3-sink --bucket prod-dd-buffer-2026 --prefix=us-east-1/$(date +%s)"
```
I'll test on one replica first.

rina: go for it. I'll tell CS that we can export buffered logs for beta-hospitality on request.

alex: tested on replica-2: starts streaming to S3, queue growth slowed. Initial rate reduction from +25k/min to +4k/min. :white_check_mark:

infra_bot: Alert: queue_size > 200k threshold breached on logship-1 (now 210k).

alex: Ok queue rose after I tested S3 on one replica. Rolling out to all replicas carefully. Applying temp filter to drop debug and verbose traces too.

cs_manager: Posted customer note to #customer-updates: "Datadog ingestion in us-east-1 is experiencing delays; we are taking mitigation steps including temporary sampling and archiving to S3. If you need immediate exports for investigations, request support." Tagged beta-hospitality + neoanalytics.

datadog-support-bot: Update: Ingestion workers redeploying. Throughput recovering slowly. Estimated recovery 40-90m. Will provide logs of impacted shards upon completion.

alex: handoff: I'm primary for mitigation now. @rina handover to monitoring to track customer impact and coordinate CS. If queue > 400k we hit critical.

rina: acknowledged; tracking active incidents and escalation.

infra_bot: New metric: dd.api.502 spikes aligned with ingestion tail. Suggest adding temporary circuit-breaker to reduce retries from agents.

tom: Good call. Reducing agent retry backoff to avoid amplifying load. Command:
```
kubectl -n observability set env daemonset/dd-agent RETRY_BACKOFF=30s
```

alex: applied retry backoff. Also increased local disk retention on forwarders (from 2GB to 5GB) to give more buffering headroom while we stream to S3.

cs_manager: beta-hospitality replied: "Thanks, want export of last 18m of logs and can wait for traces to catch up." I offered to export whichever buffered logs we have and share S3 link.

alex: attaching support ticket details to Datadog: "Ticket: DD-8901 - us-east-1 ingestion latency/backlog. Forwarder queues and agent retry spike observed. We enabled S3 sink for temporary archiving. Request detailed timeline and confirmation when shards fully recover."

datadog-support-bot: Acknowledged. Engineers will provide shard-level status in next update.

tom: note for handoff: I'll monitor Datadog status page and keep watch for ETA changes. @alex please escalate to me if queue growth > 350k.

alex: will do. Current queue 260k after full rollout of S3 sink and sampling. Growth rate ~+2k/min. Memory stable.

infra_bot: Scheduled watch: alert ops channel if queue growth > 10k/15m or if dashboards stale > 12m.

alex: quick debrief log for incident timeline:
- 1766009876: dd ingest latency alert received
- 1766009952: initial checks, queue observed at ~123k
- 1766010100: Datadog ETA 35-70m reported
- 1766010305: S3 sink enabled on replica-2 test
- 1766010450: S3 sink rolled to all replicas; sampling applied
- 1766010800: queue peaked 270k; now 260k and stabilizing

rina: creating follow-up task to add provider-ingest-failure runbook: include S3 sink steps, agent retry backoff, and fallback mapping to prometheus.

cs_manager: closing loop with beta-hospitality: they accepted S3 export. I'll coordinate transfer and log deletion policy.

datadog-support-bot: Update: ingestion workers recovering; backlog draining. ETA updated to 30-60m.

alex: handing off primary to tom for monitoring window. I'm available if Datadog asks for forwarder logs or we need to toggle sampling levels.

tom: taking over. Will ping if anything changes. Thanks everyone.

incident-bot: Incident status: observing - assigned to tom - severity P2. :white_circle:

(emoji reactions: :raised_hands: by cs_manager, :eyes: by rina)
